It then derives $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}[(RF_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(RF_{\boldsymbol s}v)]=(u*v)/S^2$ in two moves, 'First, $R$ passes through $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$' and 'Second, $R$ only moves entries', exactly as in the proof of Lemma chirp-permutation (paper lines 3953-3983).

items.note: As the assignment asks, the page only states $QF_{\boldsymbol t}w=\overline a\cdot\frac{a*(\overline a\cdot w)}{T}$ with the right $a_{\boldsymbol j}$ and links the Bluestein chirp page. Its remark that 'The factor $s_i$ in the chirp's exponent performs the frequency change of $Q$' agrees with the paper's coefficient computation.

The page writes out the Fourier sum with the substitution $h=ck$ ('which runs over every residue modulo $q$ once as $k$ does') and reaches $(F^+_qz)_{c^{-1}j}=(R_c^{-1}F^+_qz)_j$. It applies this with $q=s_i$, $c=t_i$ (a unit since $\gcd(s_i,t_i)=1$) on every coordinate to get $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=R^{-1}F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, hence $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$, as in the paper. The worked example $s_1=3$, $t_1=8$ checks out: $R$ swaps entries 1 and 2, and $e^{2\pi i(2j)(2h)/3}=e^{2\pi ijh/3}$.

The page notes that 'R only moves entries', so $R$ commutes with the pointwise product, and applies $RF^+_{\boldsymbol s}R=F^+_{\boldsymbol s}$. It then combines $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$ to get $\frac1SF^+_{\boldsymbol s}F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=\frac{u*v}{S^2}$. These are the paper's steps and normalizations, and I checked both against the paper's 1/q-normalized $F_q$ and $F_q^+$.
